It can be tough to understand, but she knows her stuff. I would say pleasant, but no nonsense. Exams can be tricky. Carefully read q's and anticipate there is a trick involved. No doubt she is the best option for 1601/1602 - I would avoid Hamdi.

Not sure why people are rating Dr. Luo so low. The class is hard, tell me about it. But she is so nice and truly wants you to pass her class. Chemistry is hard, but she tries very hard to make you learn as much as you can.

Dr. Luo was an amazing teacher. She really cares about her students and wants you to succeed. She offers a lot of help when you are confused. The homework and quizzes for this class weren't too bad, but be prepared for pretty tough exams!

analysis.name: Jinsong Zhang
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Zhang knows his stuff pretty well, and his lecture PowerPoint slides are not bad. He synthesizes the textbook pretty well and is usually available for office hours. The homework grader is pretty picky, so do the homework carefully over the weekend. Keep up and study, lots of quizzes! You can get an A if you really work for it.

The midterm carries a very heavy weight but contains very few questions, meaning that making a mistake on a single problem can destroy your final grade. The final project's grading is based completely on the professor's personal preferences rather than any clear or transparent criteria. Expect attendance right before/after breaks or final class.

Punitive grader and very unforgiving of any mistakes. Small mistakes can cost 20–30 points and late policies are heavily penalised. Because assignments with penalties can't be dropped, missing even one can significantly impact your final grade.

Numerical calculation matters the most. I'm pretty sure he'll give full credits even without any step by step solution as long as you get the "correct final answer". He doesn't give credits for understanding i.e. set up equations the correct way but make calculation mistake? -30 points.

I recommend taking CSE 417 rather than Zhang's ESE 417. Zhang gives droll, useless lectures. He gives frequent in-class quizzes that are graded strictly, he does not tolerate notation that does not match his own. Additionally, he times attendance checks just before breaks to ensure students can't go home early. He is an unkind, unhelpful teacher.

He's a pretty good professor, but his lectures are a bit boring. If you're going to take intermediate micro, take calc 3 first. Exams are exactly like practice tests.

I really enjoyed this course. Although lectures might get a bit boring sometimes, I think Weinstein explains the concepts fairly well. The homework is slightly challenging, but exams are relatively easy as they are almost identical to past papers.

Professor Weinstein is a hidden gem of the econ department. The class I had with him was well taught and fairly graded. I learned a lot of material without ever feeling too stressed. Attending class does help your grade, but I actually really enjoyed attending class, he makes econ fun and exciting.

Jonathan Weinstein is not only a great professor:  He's a great man.  But in all seriousness he's the sweetest, nerdiest guy who wants his students to succeed.  Exams are all easy; mostly identical to the homework and past exams.  Definitely take a class with him.

review_highlights.comment: Prof Schaefer is seriously the greatest! Everyone comes to his sections regardless of what class they are actually enrolled in. Even if you don't like math go sit in a few of his classes!

The hw is not too bad, but the quizzes/tests will be difficult, so make sure you attend your discussion sections, as often the quizzes will be based more on those than the hw.

Schaefer is the darling of the WashU math department for a reason! Excellent at explaining abstract concepts, good at drawing 3D diagrams, and fun lectures. Down-to-earth and fun to talk to, especially if you sit in the front! Genuinely cares about his students. Homework is difficult, but exams are always very fair. By far the best for Calc 2 & 3

Not only is he an engaging lecturer for Calc II and Calc III, but his course structuring makes it so easy for students to succeed. review_highlights.comment: student asked him to post a blank of the midterm to help study and this guy say "ill think about it" WHAT IS THERE TO THINK ABOUT

Smiles all day long and you'll be smiling with him until you realize that nothing he teaches is on the exam. analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Sayili is awesome. Super kind and is really invested in his students success. The class isn't too difficult as long as you keep up. He's been my fav prof at WashU and I'd highly recommend for any FIN course

I took Financial Management with Professor Koray and couldn't be happier. His lectures were clear and easy to follow. He challenged us with assignments and exams, but he was fair with grades and gave helpful feedback. He also knows how to support and work with international students, so if you are planning to take FIN5203, I highly recommend him!

One midterm (easier) and one final (harder) - both are MCQ. Exams are open book and you can use Excel. Group assignments are tricky but he helps a lot if you go to his office hours (and he holds plenty). His slides are well organized. He is understanding if you have an excuse not to attend. Overall good course and a good prof but not an easy A one.

Prof. Sayili is a great lecturer and he cares a lot about his students. Definitely go to his office hours as he goes above and beyond to help you. There are two group assignments and a group presentation. He takes attendance and he starts each discussion session with a quiz. If you skim the case studies, you can answer the questions easily.

I highly recommend taking VC methods with Sayili if you want to start your own venture. He covers many interesting subjects, and he does not give any exams. Definitely stop by his office if you have any questions about group projects or if want to chat about your venture ideas. He genuinely cares and goes the extra mile for his students.

I really like his teaching style. Mostly chalk w some ppt for pictures and plots. He genuinely cares that we are learning. HS were great for discussing topics.

Baril is a great teacher and the readings and learning checks are very rewarding as they often come up in other classes. The grading scale makes it easier for students to get a good grade. The final project is all up to you and besides the beginning module, the class is very interesting.
